en: Simple machines do not reduce total work; they reduce the effort force needed by spreading that work over a longer distance.
Friction does not always slow objects down; it actually helps you walk forward by pushing your shoes against the ground.
Without air resistance, a heavy bowling ball and a light marble dropped from the same height hit the ground at exactly the same time.
Magnets attract not only iron but also two other metals: nickel and cobalt.
A switch does not produce electricity; it merely opens or closes the pathway that lets current flow through a circuit.
Light travels only in straight lines and cannot bend around objects, which is why a solid wall creates a dark shadow behind it.
Sound cannot travel through the vacuum of outer space because it requires a material like air, water, or steel to carry its vibrations.
Thermal energy always moves from a hotter object to a cooler one, so ice cools your drink by absorbing heat from it.
Energy is never created or destroyed; a battery simply converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy that powers a flashlight.
A longer, gently sloping ramp requires less pushing force to raise a heavy box than a short, steep ramp of the same height.
A bar magnet pulls strongest at its two ends, called poles, and weakest at its middle section.
Earth's gravity still pulls on astronauts in orbit; they float because they and their spacecraft are continuously falling together around Earth.
